source.title: Unveiling Mode Connectivity in Graph Neural Network
source.authors: Bing-Heng Li; Zhi-Kai Chen; Hao-Yu Han; Sheng-Lai Zeng; Jing-Zhe Liu; Ji-Liang Tang

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, though the conference citation contains placeholder metadata and some appendix references are incomplete.
record.tranche_reason: Measures whether mode-connectivity metrics track the train–test generalization gap, using a different measure from the claim versions; it does not test their specific interventions or properties.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that the training-accuracy barrier correlates more strongly with the generalization gap than validation accuracy. Other claims about mode connectivity and graph properties do not measure the claim's stated outcomes. Figure 6 gives no numerical correlation values in the text.
record.test_reason: The study measures GNN mode connectivity and its association with generalization, but none of V1–V8. Its barrier between trained minima is not V7's tolerance to magnitude-scaled weight perturbations; it also does not compare that measure with norm- and margin-based measures.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the Section 4.1 finding and its proposed checkpoint-selection application, but incompletely summarizes the paper. The authors principally conclude that GNN minima often have nonlinear mode connectivity governed mainly by graph structure, and link connectivity to generalization and graph-domain discrepancy. Checkpoint selection and overfitting mitigation are suggested applications, not demonstrated interventions.
record.recipe_differences: Uses mode-connectivity barriers and their correlation with the generalization gap, rather than the interventions and measures in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported correlation comparison is limited to the analysis summarized in Figure 6; its model and dataset conditions are not stated in the text.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.1 reports that the training-accuracy barrier correlates more strongly with the generalization gap than validation accuracy. The supplied text gives no coefficients or Figure 6 model/dataset breakdown.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A mode-connectivity training-accuracy barrier can track GNN generalization gaps more strongly than validation accuracy in the tested node-classification setting.

record.peer_reviewed: Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (venue stated; citation metadata contains placeholders)
record.problems: Figure 6 has no numerical correlation values in the text. The text does not identify the models and datasets represented by each point or report uncertainty for the correlation comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for Figure 6 correlation coefficients because the text provides no values to assign. Other mode-connectivity and domain-adaptation results do not measure outcomes named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance held-out accuracy under random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification test error and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout's effects on held-out error across training-set sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps among comparably fitted convolutional networks, including ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized training examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The GNN–MLP comparisons concern connectivity barriers on graph data, not V3's image-classification advantage. The supplied manuscript's placeholder venue metadata does not establish peer-review status.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error across network widths beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected test error and local connectivity.
Large-batch versus small-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and its comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Effects of removing memorized examples on test accuracy.

rows.subject: GNN trained models (each data point represents a trained model; model and dataset breakdown not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Compared correlation of training-accuracy barrier and validation accuracy with the generalization gap.
rows.measure: Correlation with generalization gap; authors state the training-accuracy barrier has stronger correlation than validation accuracy.
rows.value: Stronger correlation than validation accuracy; numerical coefficients are figure only.
rows.note: The text does not give correlation coefficients or identify the models and datasets represented in Figure 6.
rows.check: The reported stronger correlation is supported by Section 4.1, but measures no claim version. Figure 6's coefficients and model/dataset breakdown are unavailable in the supplied text.

rows.subject: GNN trained models (each data point represents a trained model; model and dataset breakdown not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Measured validation accuracy's correlation with the generalization gap as a comparator to the training-accuracy barrier.
rows.measure: Correlation with generalization gap, compared with training-accuracy barrier.
rows.value: Weaker correlation than training-accuracy barrier; numerical coefficients are figure only.
rows.note: The text reports a relative comparison but gives no numerical correlation coefficients.
rows.check: A weaker correlation than another metric does not establish a partial claim effect. This is the comparator side of R1's comparison, and neither metric measures a listed version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
